steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Safe dance practice protects dancers from injury and supports long-term health and performance

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A warm-up gradually raises the heart rate, increases blood flow to muscles and prepares the body for dance

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: An effective warm-up includes pulse-raising activities, joint mobilisation, dynamic stretching and dance-specific movements

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: A cool-down gradually returns the body to a resting state and helps prevent stiffness and soreness

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: Name the four components of an effective warm-up. | Q: Why is a cool-down important after dancing? | Q: What is the difference between a sprain and a strain?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Pulse-raising activities, joint mobilisation, dynamic stretching and dance-specific movement preparation. | A cool-down gradually lowers the heart rate, prevents blood pooling, reduces muscle soreness and maintains flexibility through static stretching. | A sprain is damage to a ligament (joint connector), usually from twisting; a strain is damage to a muscle or tendon, usually from overstretching or overuse.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Remember the four stages of a warm-up in order: pulse raiser, joint mobilisation, dynamic stretching, dance-specific preparation When discussing injury, always name the type (sprain or strain) and link it to a dance-specific cause Nutrition answers should mention specific food groups and their function, not just 'eat healthily' Safe practice questions often require you to connect environment, personal care and rehearsal management Use the term 'progressive overload' when explaining how to build rehearsal intensity safely over time
